November 28 33.

Dear Mr. Early,

I forward herewith for your information a
tabulated statement relating to the arrest by the
Municipal Police of a Communist named Yang Shu-tang
(楊樹棠) alias Lao Tang (老唐) at No. 110 Joong
Li (中里), East Hubert Road at 11 p.m. November 16,
1933.

The accused appeared on remand before the
Second Branch of the Tingpu High Court on November 21,
1933 when he was extradited to the Chinese Authorities.

A list of the literature seized is attached.

Yours truly,

Monsieur A. Early,
Chief of the Political Section,
French Police Headquarters.

REPORT

Subject (in full) Arrest by the Municipal Police of a Chinese communist
named Yang Ts Daung.

Made by D.S. Jones Forwarded by [签名]

During the afternoon of November 17 the communist
prisoner, Yang Ts Daung (楊樹南), arrested by the Municipal
Police on November 16 was further interrogated by the undersigned
regarding the communistic literature found in his room at
No. 23 Pau Loong Li (宝隆里), East Yuhang Road at the time of
his arrest and his associations with other members of the
Chinese Communist Youth League.

Although questioned closely the accused refused to admit
that he was ever concerned with any subversive movement in the
International Settlement and adhered to his statement that he
was acting under the orders of Siau Hsu (小许), Inspector of
The Kiangsu Provincial Committee of the Chinese Communist Youth
League, these orders being that he keep in touch with members
of Communist "cells" in factories, wharves etc at Pootung.

When asked what he knew about Dah Hyi (大喜), whose
name is mentioned in a post-card found among the communistic
literature seized during the raid, Yang Ts Daung alleged that
this man is Clerk of the Pootung District Committee of the Communist
Youth League and that he first met him through Siau Hsu on the
N.Y.K. Wharf near the Japanese Consulate a few weeks ago. He
met Dah Hyi alone at the same place three or four times after
this and discussed with him the possibilities of enlarging the
Communist "cell" at Lau Bah Doo (老白渡) Wharf, Pootung. Dah
Hyi also advised him as the the best method to keep in contact
with the various Pootung "cells" and to supply them posters
bearing communist slogans (vide specimens attached). According
the the prisoner there are at present five comrades in the Lau
Bah Doo "cell".

Description of Dah Hyi : age about 25, native of Kempo,

Yang Ts Daung (楊樹堂)
Chensl D. . Jones
Kashing Rd tn Nov.16, 1933 Clerk K.L.Pang

My name is Yang Ts Daung(楊樹堂). I was born at Han Chung
Heien (漢中県). Chensi. 1909. My father, who was formerly Chief
of the Education Bureau at my native place, is now unemployed. At
the age of 12 I began to attend the primary school at Han Chung
Heien and remained there as a pupil until I was 20, when I left
school. For the next 3 years I was unemployed and stayed at home.
In December 1932 I came to Shanghai to resume my studies.
I intended entering the Vung Hua (文化) College, Kiangwan, but as
I brought with me only $100 and spent $80 in travelling expenses,
I was unable to realise my ambition owing to the fact that the
entrance fee to this college is $80.
From December 1932 until October 1933 I lived at No. 108
Vung 'a Road (永欣路), Kiangwan. For my room I paid $4.50 per
mensem. During this period I was unemployed and spent my leisure
hours reading newspapers and books. I was able to subsist on
remittance received from home.
On October 15 this year a man named Tiau Hsu (小許) came
to see me at the instance of my friend Tsang Yoh Ching (張約清),
a student at Vung Hua College. The latter was formerly a communist
but has now severed his connection with the Party.
Tiau Hsu, who told me he was a communist, persuaded me to
join the Pootung District Committee of the Chinese Communist
Youth League. I joined and was appointed a member of the
propaganda section at a salary of $8 a month. Ten days ago
Tiau Hsu paid me $2. Since then he has paid me $6 in two
instalments. The last time he visited me was on the 13th inst.
I have visited various cells in factories situated in

(Page 2)

Pootung to instruct the workers in propaganda work for the
Chinese Communist Youth League.

The Communist literature and posters found in the room
at the time of my arrest were brought by Tiau Hsu on November 10
My instructions from Tiau Hsu were to study the literature and
to distribute the posters among "red" cells in the Pootung
factories.

Tiau Hsu is an inspector of the Kiangsu Provincial
Committee of the Chinese Communist Youth League. He never
divulged to me his address and I do not know where he can be
located.

(Signed) Yang Ts Daung.
